newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ekeus to leave U.N. job on Iraq on July 1.
newsitem.headline: Ekeus to leave U.N. job on Iraq on July 1.

text.p: Rolf Ekeus, the head of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, said he would be leaving his United Nations post on July 1.

Speaking informally to reporters, Ekeus said his new job as the Swedish ambassador to Washington was not officially announced but he expected to leave the United Nations on July 1 after six years on the job.

Ekeus spoke after briefing the Security Council members on his latest report on Iraqi disarmament. He said that members "did not want a change of direction" and that the commission should continue "with the same energy."

One possible candidate to replace Ekeus was Emilio Cardenas, Argentina's former ambassador to the United Nations, who has returned to the private sector in Buenos Aires. He was interviewed for the post in mid-January.

Other candidates, diplomats said, include Richard Butler, Australia's ambassador to the United Nations, Pasi Patokallio, Finland's. deputy director general for foreign affairs and currently chairman of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty conference and Johan Molander of Sweden, chairman of the conference negotiating a possible ban on landmines.
The U.N. Speciai Commission is in charge of ridding Iraq of weapons of mass destruction -- including nuclear warheads, biological and chemical arms and ballistic missiles.
Sanctions against Iraq, imposed after it invaded Kuwait in 1990, cannot be lifted until the commission is satisfied it has accounted for all the dangerous weapons.
